item.content:encoded:
数字 · 出门生存句 (Numbers & Survival — shop, order, find your way)

Chinese numbers are a machine you learn once: count 1–10 and every price, time and phone number unlocks. Plus ordering, bargaining and finding the toilet — English + ខ្មែរ support, native audio on every line.

The big picture

After ten, Chinese numbers are pure Lego: 11 is 'ten-one', 20 is 'two-ten', 123 is 'one-hundred-two-ten-three'. No new words ever — just slots you already know.

  • 一二三四五六七八九十: Ten sounds, that's the whole alphabet of numbers
  • 十一 = 10+1: 11–19: ten, then the digit
  • 二十 = 2×10: 20, 30, 40…: digit, then ten
  • 多少钱？: Two words unlock every market
  • 我要…: 'I want' orders anything, anywhere
  • 两 vs 二: Two before things is liǎng, not èr

The text · an afternoon out, start to finish

一到十 · One to ten
一 yī 二 èr 三 sān 四 sì 五 wǔ 六 liù 七 qī 八 bā 九 jiǔ 十 shí。
One to ten. Tap Listen and repeat each in your head — the tones are the workout.

大数 · Bigger numbers
十一 shíyī = 11，二十 èrshí = 20，一百 yìbǎi = 100。 数东西用“两”：两个人 liǎng ge rén，不說二个人。
11 is 'ten-one', 20 is 'two-ten', 100 is 'one-hundred'. The machine never stops. Before counted things use 两 (liǎng): 'two people' is 两个人. 二 is for counting and math.

价钱 · Money & prices
这个多少钱？Zhège duōshao qián? 八十块 bāshí kuài = ¥80。“块”是口语的“元”。
How much is this? — the two magic words of every market in China. Eighty kuài = ¥80. Spoken Chinese says 块 where prices print 元.

点单 · Ordering
我要一杯咖啡。Wǒ yào yì bēi kāfēi.
I'd like one cup of coffee. Swap in anything: 我要茶, 我要水.

找路 · Finding places
请问，洗手间在哪儿？Qǐng wèn, xǐshǒujiān zài nǎr? 电话号码一个数字一个数字读：138，0201。
Excuse me, where is the toilet? 在 = at, 哪儿 = where. Phone numbers are read digit by digit — just the ten sounds you already know.

Q&A

Traps · read these first

Q. “十”和“四”老听混，怎么办？ (I keep confusing shí (10) and sì (4). Help?)
A. 十是第二声，往上走；四是第四声，往下砸。用手画音高。 (十 rises (tone 2), 四 falls hard (tone 4). Draw the pitch in the air with your hand while listening.)

Q. 什么时候用“两”，什么时候用“二”？ (When 两 and when 二?)
A. 东西前用两：两个人、两杯。数数和电话号码用二。 (两 before counted things (两个人, 两杯); 二 for counting sequences and phone numbers.)

Q. 价格说“块”还是“元”？ (Do people say kuài or yuán for prices?)
A. 口语说块，菜单写元。意思一样：一百块 = 100 元。 (Spoken: 块. Printed menus: 元. Same money — 一百块 = ¥100.)

Real conversations

Q. 这个多少钱？——八十块。 (How much? — Eighty yuan.)
A. 太贵了！便宜一点，行吗？ (Too expensive! A little cheaper, OK? (markets: always ask once, smiling))

Q. 你要几个？ (How many do you want?)
A. 两个，谢谢。 (Two, please. (number + 个 + nothing — the default measure word))

Q. 现在几点？ (What time is it now?)
A. 现在三点。三点一刻 / 三点半。 (It's three. 三点一刻 = 3:15, 三点半 = 3:30.)

When you get stuck

太贵了。 (Too expensive.)

好吃！ (Delicious!)

我听不懂。 (I don't understand (what I hear).)

Patterns · the number machine

Q. 三 + 个 + 人 (Pattern: Number + measure word + noun — three people.)
A. 两杯水、三个人、四个苹果。 (Two cups of water, three people, four apples. 个 works when you're unsure.)

Q. 现在三点。 (Pattern: time words are just numbers — 点 o'clock, 半 half.)
A. 八点上课，十二点吃饭。 (Class at 8, lunch at 12. No verb needed.)

Q. 洗手间在哪儿？ (Pattern: Thing + 在哪儿? = 'Where is …?')
A. 厕所在哪儿？地铁站在哪儿？ (Where's the toilet? Where's the metro station?)

Vocabulary (27)

1–10 · the whole alphabet
一 yī: one
二 èr: two (counting)
三 sān: three
四 sì: four
五 wǔ: five
六 liù: six
七 qī: seven
八 bā: eight
九 jiǔ: nine
十 shí: ten

The machine · bigger numbers
十一 shíyī: eleven (ten-one)
二十 èrshí: twenty (two-ten)
一百 yìbǎi: one hundred
一千 yìqiān: one thousand
两 liǎng: two (before things)

Money · at the stall
钱 qián: money
块 kuài: yuan (spoken)
元 yuán: yuan (printed)
多少钱 duōshao qián: how much?
贵 guì: expensive
便宜 piányi: cheap

Out and about
要 yào: to want
咖啡 kāfēi: coffee
茶 chá: tea
好吃 hǎochī: tasty
洗手间 xǐshǒujiān: toilet, washroom
这儿 / 那儿 zhèr / nàr: here / there

item.title: 打招呼 · 介绍自己 (Greetings & Introductions — speak on day one)
item.description: The ten phrases that open every Chinese conversation: hello, how are you, your name, nice to meet you, thanks and goodbye — English + ខ្មែរ support, native Mandarin audio on every line. 10 picture cards, 9 questions, 22 words.
item.content:encoded:
打招呼 · 介绍自己 (Greetings & Introductions — speak on day one)

The ten phrases that open every Chinese conversation: hello, how are you, your name, nice to meet you, thanks and goodbye — English + ខ្មែរ support, native Mandarin audio on every line.

The big picture

A first meeting in Chinese is a fixed little dance of five moves. Learn one line per move and you can hold the whole conversation — no grammar needed yet.

  • 你好: One hello fits almost every situation
  • 您: Add 心 at the bottom = respect
  • 我叫…: State your name with 叫
  • 很高兴认识你: The standard 'nice to meet you'
  • 再见 / 明天见: Bye, or the friendlier 'see you tomorrow'
  • 请: One word offers, invites and softens

The text · one first meeting, start to finish

见面 · Saying hello
你好！Nǐ hǎo — 最常用的打招呼。 对长辈、客户说：您好！Nín hǎo。 你好吗？Nǐ hǎo ma — 问别人怎么样。
Hello! Works with almost anyone, anywhere. Say 您好 (nín hǎo) to elders, teachers and customers — it carries respect. How are you? A real question, but friends often skip it.

名字 · Names
我叫 + 名字：我叫 Dara。 请问，你叫什么名字？Qǐng wèn…
'My name is …' — literally 'I am-called Dara'. Put your name right after 叫. 'May I ask your name?' — start with 请问 to sound polite.

回答 · Answering
我很好，谢谢。Wǒ hěn hǎo, xiè xie. 很高兴认识你！Hěn gāoxìng rènshi nǐ.
I'm very well, thank you — the standard bright answer. Nice to meet you! Say it right after names are exchanged.

再见 · Saying goodbye
再见！Zàijiàn — 或者更自然：明天见！
Goodbye! Even more natural with people you'll see again: 'See you tomorrow'.

礼貌 · Being polite
请坐，请喝茶，请先走 — 一个“请”走遍中国。 别人帮你：谢谢！他说：不客气。
Please sit, please have tea, after you — one 请 softens everything. Someone helps: xiè xie (thank you). The reply is 不客气 — 'you're welcome'.

Q&A

Traps · read these first

Q. 什么时候用“您”？ (When do I use the polite 您?)
A. 长辈、老师、客户、第一次见的客人。朋友用你。 (Elders, teachers, customers, guests you just met. With friends, plain 你.)

Q. “吃了吗？”是要请我吃饭吗？ (Is 'Have you eaten?' an invitation to dinner?)
A. 不是，那只是打招呼。回答：吃了，你呢？ (No — it's just a greeting among friends. Answer: 吃了，你呢? (Yes, and you?))

Q. 打电话第一句说什么？ (What do I say first on a phone call?)
A. 电话里说“喂”（wéi），然后说自己是谁。 (On the phone Chinese says 喂 (wéi), then your own name — not 你好.)

Real conversations

Q. 你叫什么名字？ (What's your name?)
A. 我叫 Dara。你呢？ (My name is Dara. And you?)

Q. 他是谁？ (Who is he?)
A. 他是我朋友，他叫 Sok。 (He's my friend. His name is Sok.)

Q. 认识你很高兴。 (Nice to meet you. (they say it first))
A. 我也很高兴认识你。 (I'm also very glad to meet you.)

When you get stuck

你会说英语吗？ (Do you speak English?)

请再说一遍。 (Please say that again.)

我先走了，再见！ (I have to go now — goodbye!)

Patterns · sound Chinese from day one

Q. 我叫 Dara。 (Pattern: 我叫 + name — 'I am called …')
A. 他叫 Sok。她叫 Malis。 (He's called Sok. She's called Malis.)

Q. 我是学生。 (Pattern: 我是 + thing — 'I am a …' (no verb change))
A. 他是老师。我们是朋友。 (He is a teacher. We are friends. 是 never conjugates.)

Q. 你呢？ (Pattern: X 呢? = 'And X?' — the fastest way to bounce a question back.)
A. 我很好，你呢？——我也很好。 (I'm well — and you? — I'm well too.)

Vocabulary (22)

Greetings · the front door
你好 nǐ hǎo: hello
您好 nín hǎo: hello (respectful)
早上好 zǎoshang hǎo: good morning
晚安 wǎn'ān: good night
再见 zàijiàn: goodbye
明天见 míngtiān jiàn: see you tomorrow

People · who is who
我 wǒ: I, me
你 nǐ: you
您 nín: you (respectful)
他 tā: he, him
她 tā: she, her
朋友 péngyou: friend
老师 lǎoshī: teacher

Words that run the conversation
叫 jiào: to be called
是 shì: to be
什么 shénme: what
谁 shéi: who
请 qǐng: please
谢谢 xiè xie: thank you
不客气 bú kèqi: you're welcome
对不起 duìbuqǐ: sorry
没关系 méi guānxi: it's OK, no problem

item.title: 声调 · 四声 (Tones First — the fast track starts here)
item.description: The one-hour foundation for speaking Mandarin: the four tones plus neutral, tone-pair drills, the tricky zh/ch/sh/r sounds and your first sentences — with English and Khmer support and native audio on every line. 6 picture cards, 8 questions, 20 words.
item.content:encoded:
声调 · 四声 (Tones First — the fast track starts here)

The one-hour foundation for speaking Mandarin: the four tones plus neutral, tone-pair drills, the tricky zh/ch/sh/r sounds and your first sentences — with English and Khmer support and native audio on every line.

The big picture

Mandarin uses pitch to tell words apart, so tones are not decoration — they ARE the word. Learn the four contours on one syllable and you can pronounce any pinyin you ever meet.

  • ā á ǎ à: The mark above the vowel is the tone
  • 妈 mā: Tone 1: high and flat, like a held note
  • 麻 má: Tone 2: rises, like 'What?'
  • 马 mǎ: Tone 3: dips low, the slowest one
  • 骂 mà: Tone 4: falls hard, like 'No!'
  • 吗 ma: Neutral tone: short and light

The text · tones, start to finish

四声 · The four tones
妈 mā · 麻 má · 马 mǎ · 骂 mà — one syllable, four different words. 吗 ma 是轻声：又短又轻。
mā mother · má hemp · mǎ horse · mà to scold. The tone changes the word. The neutral tone (ma) is short and light — no mark above the vowel.

组合 · Tone pairs
两个第三声连在一起，第一个读第二声：你好 → ní hǎo。
When two third tones meet, the first becomes a second: 你好 is read 'ní hǎo'.

难音 · Tricky sounds
zh、ch、sh、r：舌尖卷起来，靠近上颚。
For zh, ch, sh and r curl the tip of your tongue up toward the roof of your mouth.

句子 · First sentences
中文句子和英语一样：主语 + 动词 + 宾语，动词不变。 陈述句 + 吗 = 一般疑问句：你喜欢咖啡 → 你喜欢咖啡吗？
Chinese word order is Subject + Verb + Object like English — and verbs never change form. Add 吗 to the end of any statement and it becomes a yes/no question.

Q&A

Traps · read these first

Q. 可以不学声调，只学拼音吗？ (Can I skip tones and just learn pinyin?)
A. 不行。妈、马不一样；声调错了，意思就变了。 (No. mā (mother) and mǎ (horse) are different words — wrong tone, wrong meaning.)

Q. 声调说错了，别人听得懂吗？ (If I get a tone wrong, will people understand me?)
A. 大多数时候能听懂。别怕，先开口，慢慢就准了。 (Usually yes — context carries you. Speak first; accuracy comes with practice.)

Q. 要先会汉字才能开口说吗？ (Do I need characters before I can speak?)
A. 不用。口语用拼音就能开始，汉字可以慢慢来。 (No. For speaking, pinyin is enough to start; learn characters slowly in parallel.)

Real questions

Q. 每天练多久，进步最快？ (How long per day is the fastest progress?)
A. 每天十五分钟，比一周一次两小时有效。 (Fifteen focused minutes every day beats two hours once a week.)

Q. 哪个声调最难？ (Which tone is the hardest?)
A. 对英语母语者，第二声和第三声最容易混。多听对比。 (For English speakers, tones 2 and 3 blur together most. Drill them as minimal pairs.)

When you get stuck

请说慢一点儿。 (Please speak a little slower.)

这个词是什么意思？ (What does this word mean?)

我还不会说。 (I can't say that yet.)

Patterns · the grammar you need today

Q. 我喜欢咖啡。 (Pattern: Subject + Verb + Object — 'I like coffee.')
A. 他喜欢茶。我们学习中文。 (He likes tea. We study Chinese. The verb never changes.)

Q. 你喜欢咖啡吗？ (Pattern: statement + 吗 = yes/no question.)
A. 你喜欢茶吗？——喜欢 / 不喜欢。 (Do you like tea? — Yes (like) / No (don't like). Answer with the verb itself.)

Q. 我不喜欢茶。 (Pattern: put 不 before the verb to say no.)
A. 我不是老师。他不去。 (I'm not a teacher. He doesn't go. 不 sits right before the verb.)

Vocabulary (20)

The ma family · hear the four tones
妈 mā: mother
麻 má: hemp; numb
马 mǎ: horse
骂 mà: to scold

Tone words in real pairs
你好 nǐ hǎo: hello (3+3 → reads 2+3)
谢谢 xiè xie: thank you (4 + neutral)
中国 Zhōngguó: China (1+2)
很便宜 hěn piányi: very cheap (3+2)

Tricky consonants · zh ch sh r ü
是 shì: to be (curl the tongue)
吃 chī: to eat (a puff of air)
十 shí: ten (rising + curl)
日 rì: day; sun (like French j)
女 nǚ: woman (say 'ee' with round lips)

First-sentence words
我 wǒ: I, me
你 nǐ: you
他 tā: he, him
喜欢 xǐhuan: to like
学习 xuéxí: to study
咖啡 kāfēi: coffee
茶 chá: tea
